# std::dsp::convolution

Module file: `stdlib/std/dsp/convolution.mla`

Linear convolution helpers for numeric [`list<T>`](Quick-Guide#types) values.

Modes:
- `full_*`: full linear convolution, output length `signal.len() + kernel.len() - 1`
- `same_*`: center-cropped convolution, output length `signal.len()`
- `valid_*`: only positions where the kernel fully overlaps the signal

API:
- `full_i64(signal: &list<i64>, kernel: &list<i64>) -> list<i64>`
- `same_i64(signal: &list<i64>, kernel: &list<i64>) -> list<i64>`
- `valid_i64(signal: &list<i64>, kernel: &list<i64>) -> list<i64>`
- `full_f32(signal: &list<f32>, kernel: &list<f32>) -> list<f32>`
- `same_f32(signal: &list<f32>, kernel: &list<f32>) -> list<f32>`
- `valid_f32(signal: &list<f32>, kernel: &list<f32>) -> list<f32>`
- `full_f64(signal: &list<f64>, kernel: &list<f64>) -> list<f64>`
- `same_f64(signal: &list<f64>, kernel: &list<f64>) -> list<f64>`
- `valid_f64(signal: &list<f64>, kernel: &list<f64>) -> list<f64>`

Empty inputs return an empty list. `valid_*` also returns an empty list when
the kernel is longer than the signal.

Example:

```rust
mod std::dsp::convolution;

use std::dsp::convolution::full_f32;
use std::dsp::convolution::same_f32;
use std::dsp::convolution::valid_f32;

let signal: list<f32> = [1.0f, 2.0f, 3.0f];
let kernel: list<f32> = [0.5f, 0.25f];

let full: list<f32> = full_f32(signal, kernel);
let same: list<f32> = same_f32(signal, kernel);
let valid: list<f32> = valid_f32(signal, kernel);
```

See [`tests/std_dsp_tests.mla`](https://github.com/mattilaa/mlang/blob/main/tests/std_dsp_tests.mla).
